title: Pattern executes operationally through an Executor Accord Instance with Ozone rather than staffing execution itself
content:
Pattern's Executor Accord Primitive is `Active` with a single named instance, the Ozone Instance (A.6.1.1.6.2.2.1.2.1). Its first parameter is not a person or a term but a pointer: A.6.1.1.6.2.2.1.2.1.1.1 says "The Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps for Ozone are specified in [A.6.1.2.2 - Operational Executor Agent Ozone]."

This is the Prime/Executor division made concrete. Pattern holds the mandate, the token and the capital; Ozone supplies the humans who operate and review. The Accord Primitive is the interface between them, and it has an ongoing "process for the ongoing management" of the instance (A.6.1.1.6.2.2.1.2.1.2) — unlike the sealed Genesis Primitives, this relationship is live and maintained.

The structural advantage is substitutability. Because the operating roles are defined in Ozone's Artifact rather than Pattern's, changing operators is a change of Accord instance, not a rewrite of the Agent. It also lets one Executor Agent serve multiple Primes, and keeps a reviewer (Operational GovOps) organizationally separate from the entity whose actions are being reviewed.

The corresponding exposure is dependency: Pattern's ability to act at all runs through an entity it does not define, so a failure or suspension on the Ozone side is an operational failure for Pattern.
description: The Ozone Instance's Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps are defined in a separate Executor Agent Artifact, so Pattern's operating personnel live outside Pattern's own Artifact.
